Allah knows best who played what role in 1971: Jamaat ameer
2026-04-09T18:51:21+06:00 | Star Online Report
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/the-parliament-watch/parliament/news/allah-knows-best-who-played-what-role-1971-jamaat-ameer-4147706

Opposition Leader and Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman today said Allah knows best who played what role during the 1971 Liberation War.

“Allah Almighty is the only perfect and complete witness. The rest of us are partial witnesses, but Allah alone is the complete witness,” he said.

The National Freedom Fighters Council (Amendment) Bill 2026 was passed in the parliament by voice vote today. Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Azam Khan presented the bill in the House. Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed asked if anyone had any objection to the bill.

At this point, the opposition leader said, “Our region has gained independence twice -- once in 1947, and then again after 23 years through the Liberation War. I pay deep respect to all those who fought bravely for the country and the nation during the great Liberation War.”

Opposition stages walkout over ‘anti-people’ bills in parliament

The Jamaat ameer said that although the country was born with “great hopes,” those aspirations were not fulfilled by the rulers at the time.

He also remarked that multi-party democracy was killed through the establishment of BAKSAL soon after independence.

“Following the political changeover of 1975, late president Ziaur Rahman undoubtedly restored multi-party democracy. The nation benefited from it in subsequent periods, and today’s parliament is part of that continuity,” the Jamaat ameer said.

Jamaat’s 'note of dissent' in the definition of Freedom Fighter

Referring to the Freedom Fighters Council (Amendment) Bill, Shafiqur said, “What has been proposed in this bill was not introduced even by those who governed after independence. Late president Ziaur Rahman did not bring it, nor did the highly respected three-time prime minister Khaleda Zia. This provision was introduced by Sheikh Hasina, a representative of fascism, and the interim government later retained that continuity with minor changes.”

The Jamaat ameer said, “What is in this bill? It mentions the names of three organisations: the then Muslim League, Jamaat-e-Islami, and Nezam-e-Islam Party. Alongside the Pakistan army and some ancillary forces, the names of these three political parties have been included, and the current proposal refers to these organisations.”

The road to liberation: March 1971 and the years that led to it

Reiterating his earlier point, he said they want every political organisation in the country to operate with a sense of responsibility and compassion towards the people.

Saying they did not want division in the nation, he added, “In 1979, the Awami League itself was revived in Bangladesh through the Political Parties Revival Act. At that time, all political parties regained the opportunity and the right to engage in politics. We, too, regained that right then.”

He expressed gratitude to Allah as well as to martyred president Ziaur Rahman, adding, “We have never forgotten this and never will. With that sense of responsibility, compassion and love, we have sought to carry out our political and organisational activities in Bangladesh since 1979. In the days ahead, let it be the commitment of all parties not to divide the nation, but to unite it, so that we may build a dignified nation that stands tall with pride.”
